newsitem.title: CHINA: Positive H2 seen for HSBC, Hang Seng.
newsitem.headline: Positive H2 seen for HSBC, Hang Seng.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc's surprisingly good first-half results and expectations of a slower but positive second half were forcing most analysts to make upward revisions for the full year.
But analysts said they don't plan to revise their 1997 earnings forecasts for Hang Seng Bank Ltd.

"They were very strong results," said John Hobson, regional banking analyst at Morgan Stanley. "We are likely to see Hang Seng Bank and HSBC use the balance sheet even more efficiently in the second half."

HSBC Holdings Plc reported operating profit before provisions of 2.57 billion sterling, a 15 percent rise over first half 1996, and an 11 percent increase in attributable profit to 1.76 billion sterling.
The bank's results fell in the middle of a wide range of forecasts and despite reductions on translation of the group's U.S.-dollar-tied Asian earnings into sterling.
"The bank actually had earnings growth of 18 percent in Hong Kong dollar terms," said an analyst with a large regional house.
"Provisions (for bad debts) were lower than expected and gains on the disposals (of investments) were higher than expected, especially after last year's," he said.
In first-half 1997, the banking giant reported gains on asset sales of 179 million sterling, a fall of 84 million sterling compared with first-half 1996.
"I am revising upward my full year forecast by four percent to HK$44.9 billion because the first half was much stronger than I'd forecast," said the analyst.
In Hong Kong dollar terms, this would be growth of 19.46 percent.
"But going forward, I think in the second half we will see slower mortgage loan growth in Hong Kong and generally slower earnings growth around the region," he said.
Analysts said the impact of volatility in regional currencies would also be felt in the second half.

Midland Bank Plc, which had a positive first half, is also forecast to see slower growth in the second half due to a an expected interest rates hike in the U.K, which will dampen credit demand, analysts said.
"Midland's results were very, very good," said analyst Shannon Garrett at SocGen Crosby Securities. "There is some concern that asset expansion has been too aggressive."
Midland Bank reported attributable profit of 512 million sterling, a 17 percent increase over the same period last year.
The consensus forecast for Hang Seng Bank is for earnings growth of 19 percent for the full year. Analysts said they had no plans to revise this figure after the interim results.
Hang Seng Bank Ltd reported operating profit before provisions of HK$5.31 billion, a 12.7 percent rise. Attributable profit rose 14.5 percent to HK$4.98 billion.
"Loan growth was quite strong but this was not reflected in net interest income growth," said the regional analyst. "And they were unable to increase trade finance by much."
This inability to grow its exposure to industries other than property did not bode well for long-term earnings growth, analysts said.

Most analysts believed the territory's year-long mortgage war would continue and keep downward pressure on margins, but that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's dim view of aggressive pricing strategies would slow volume growth.
